question: Dot-product attention and additive attention have about the same theoretical cost. Why is scaled dot-product still preferred in practice, and why divide by √d_k when d_k is large?
raw_answer: Scaled dot-product attention is preferred in practice because it is much faster and more space-efficient than additive attention, as it can be implemented using highly optimized matrix multiplication code [[cite:e8118712b3430e7a]]. The dot products are scaled by $1/\sqrt{d_k}$ to counteract the effect of large $d_k$ values, which cause dot products to grow large in magnitude and push the softmax function into regions where it has extremely small gradients [[cite:e8118712b3430e7a]].
